flows.narrative: No fresher weekly fund-flow data has been published since the week ended 11 Nov -- the same cut already baked into yesterday's file. BofA/EPFR logged global equity inflows of +$98.3bn that week (largest since June 2026, led by a 6th-straight-week +$63.6bn US inflow and a 5th-straight-week China inflow) alongside a -$17.9bn money-market outflow; Reuters/LSEG Lipper's larger fund universe instead showed Europe as the week's biggest single draw (+$35.13bn, strongest since June 2021) with US equities +$6.6bn and EM equities +$4.65bn, plus a -$37.48bn money-market reversal. ICI's independently-sourced money-market series corroborates the cash outflow direction (-$35.72bn in total MMF assets for the week ended 11 Nov, after +$117.97bn the week before). Both equity-flow trackers agree gold ETF flows stayed modestly positive even as the gold price fell toward 14-month lows. None of this yet reflects the Mon-Wed 16-18 Nov selloff (S&P -1.92%/-1.03%/-0.50%, VIX spiking to ~25 before easing to 24.69) or the miner-specific unwind in GDX/SILJ; the next weekly cuts (due ~19-20 Nov) remain the ones to watch for the first read on whether this was a genuine flow reversal or a sentiment-only move.
